title: WORKPLACE BULLYING
mv: Therefore all things whatsoever ye would that men should do to you, do ye even so to them: for this is the law and the prophets.
mvp: “Therefore all things whatsoever ye would that men should do to you, do ye even so to them: for this is the law and the prophets.” Matthew 7:12
assignment: Have you experienced workplace bullying? If yes, identify someone currently going through workplace bullying and use your knowledge and the lessons you learned from this study to help such (No mark).

b.x: In workplaces, many people face subtle or open behaviours that intimidate, belittle, or humiliate them. Such conduct is bullying and can come from anyone, e.g. supervisors, co-workers, subordinates, etc. It often begins as a desire to control, but eventually causes deep emotional wounds and disunity in the organisation. As followers of Christ, we are called to a higher standard of love and respect (Philippians 2:3; Romans 12:21). When we live out these commands, we not only resist the spirit of bullying but also become lights of grace and peace in our workplaces (Matthew 5:16).

Workplace bullying can take many forms and often begins with verbal comments that mentally hurt or isolate a person (1 Samuel 1:6). This creates an atmosphere of fear and division. Sometimes, workplace bullying is not immediately obvious. It can be subtle and hidden, such as deliberately excluding someone from decisions, conversations, or work-related events. Other tactics include ignoring someone’s opinions, making them feel useless, or being assigned unpleasant tasks, all of which erode confidence and dignity. Workplace bullying is not limited to face-to-face encounters. It can occur through written communication, phone calls, or email, allowing harmful actions to spread beyond the physical workplace.

There is also what is known as “upward bullying,” which may involve showing continuous disrespect, refusing to complete tasks, spreading rumours, undermining authority or making a leader appear incompetent. Absalom bullied his father, King David, into going into exile (2Samuel 15:1-14).

Workplace bullying, when left unchecked, gradually damages the reputation of a company, making it difficult to retain and attract high-performing employees (Proverbs 14:34). This toxic environment discourages collaboration, weakens morale and prevents employees from effectively navigating challenges.

For individuals, the effects of workplace bullying can be deeply damaging to both work performance and personal well-being (Proverbs 12:25). Victims may become less productive from lack of motivation, reduced job satisfaction and confidence in their abilities, and experience constant headaches, backaches, and sleep problems. It can result in serious mental health issues such as fear, deep distress, depression and suicidal thoughts (Proverbs 15:13).

Handling workplace bullying requires a deliberate effort to create a supportive and respectful environment. Expectations for appropriate behaviour should be clearly set and communicated to all staff (Habakkuk 2:2). A culture of respect, open communication, teamwork, and feedback should be fostered (1 Thessalonians 5:11). There should be provision of a safe and confidential reporting system where employees can raise concerns without fear (Isaiah 1:17; Matthew 18:15). All complaints should be taken seriously, investigated thoroughly, and addressed promptly (Zechariah 7:9). Supervisors and managers should be trained to recognise signs of bullying, handle complaints fairly, and act swiftly, whether or not a formal complaint has been made (Leviticus 19:35a).

Employees can take proactive steps to protect themselves. Consulting a trusted colleague or mentor, documenting incidents in detail, and resolving issues directly or with managerial support can be effective (Proverbs 27:9). When supporting a colleague who is being bullied, it is important to listen empathetically but also maintain objectivity, encouraging them to seek the right assistance rather than fuelling gossip (Ephesians 4:29). Good communication skills, resilience and self-awareness are keys in managing these situations (Judges 8:1-3; Proverbs 15:1).
Individuals must prioritise their mental, spiritual and physical health (3 John 2).
